title: groundstation field test №20: 5 asks Danny brought, Mt St Helens 1980, Hurricane Patricia 2015, the Swiss glaciers, the Eagle Creek fire 2017 and Portland right now
heading: THE FIELD TEST №20
sub: groundstation · 5 prompts · 5 live artifacts · 2 works, 3 partly, 0 not yet · October 27, 2026 · Development Seed labs
lede: These 5 cards are the README's front-page examples. The old 3 had no source in any field test: an audit found their numbers nowhere in docs/, so they are replaced by real asks about places Danny knows, with every number on the README quoted from a card below. 2 of the 5 run on Landsat: Mt St Helens in 1980, years before Sentinel-2, on Landsat 2 and 3 MSS scenes, and Hurricane Patricia in 2015 on Landsat 8. The Eagle Creek fire of 2017 is the one card that can use compare_dates, since Sentinel-2 on Earth Search reaches 2017. Portland asks the live feeds about today. Each learning opens with what the tools could do for the ask: Works, Partly or Not yet. Run on main at 0.59.0.

cases.answer: The 1980 eruption is in reach: Landsat 2 and 3 MSS scenes from the same orbit (path 50, row 28), 1979-09-12 and 1980-09-15, both 0.0% cloud and covering 100.0% of the box, and the median vegetation index over the box fell from 0.2691 to -0.0043. describe_collection says landsat-c2-l1 holds MSS scenes from Landsat 1 to 5, 1972 to 2013, and landsat-c2-l2 starts on 1982-08-22, so the L1 collection is the only one here that reaches 1980. The collection lists 4 bands: green, red, nir08 and nir09. Spring 1980 has no clear scene (6 scenes, 42.0% to 98.0% cloud), so the before is the summer of 1979, one year and 3 days before the after. On the index (nir08-red)/(nir08+red), the mean over the 0.30 by 0.20 degree box went from 0.2397 to 0.0737 and the median from 0.2691 to -0.0043. compare_dates could not be used ("0 after, 0 before"): it searches only Earth Search Sentinel-2. The index is on top-of-atmosphere radiance, so it is not comparable with a modern NDVI. The swipe map draws both MSS scenes in false colour; left of the divider the 1980 scene shows a grey blast zone north and west of the crater, and right of it the 1979 scene shows red forest and a snow-capped peak (my reading of the image).
cases.artifact_label: map: Mt St Helens swipe, 1979-09-12 against 1980-09-15 ↗
cases.learning: Works. The catalog confirmed the 1972 MSS archive from describe_collection, not from memory; search_imagery returned 20 summer scenes each year, the limit asked for; compute_statistics and render_map both took landsat-c2-l1 items as they are. The one tool that could not help is compare_dates, which has no collection argument and searches Earth Search sentinel-2-l2a only (that is in its code; the output is the plain "Not enough scenes" error, not a reason). 2 things to know about the figure. First, the scaling compute_statistics applied is the item's own, and its unit is watt/steradian/square_meter/micrometer: this is an index on top-of-atmosphere radiance, not surface reflectance, so it is not comparable to a Landsat 8 or Sentinel-2 NDVI, and the 2 scenes come from 2 sensors (Landsat 2 and Landsat 3) with different gains. Second, the box holds forest, lakes and the cone, so the drop of 0.2734 in the median is the whole box, not the blast zone alone. Not checked: the share of the box that went from vegetated to bare (the tools give no per-pixel threshold count), sun angle and haze between 1979-09-12 and 1980-09-15, and the qa_pixel band. The first screenshot had the 1979 layer stop partway across the east and south of the frame; a retake with 8 more seconds after network idle drew it to the edges, so that was tiles still loading, not the scene's footprint.
cases.shows: describe_collection confirms MSS from 1972 · landsat-c2-l2 starts 1982-08-22 · band ids green, red, nir08, nir09 · no clear spring 1980 scene · compare_dates is Sentinel-2 only · median index 0.2691 to -0.0043 · swipe map of 2 MSS scenes

cases.answer: Landsat 8 has the coast on 2015-10-13, 10 days before landfall, and on 2015-11-30, 38 days after, and the median vegetation index over the land box fell from 0.8712 to 0.8226, but the after scene is cloudier, so damage and cloud are not separated; the event feeds hold only current events and do not reach 2015. Both catalogs carry landsat-c2-l2 for 2015 and return the same 16 post-landfall ids. I kept to one Landsat 8 path and row (030047) on both dates: before at 11.6% cloud, after at 18.53% cloud, both covering 100.0% of the box. The first statistics box takes in ocean and its index ran from -1921 to 3894, so I moved to a smaller box further east, over land ([-104.98, 19.38, -104.82, 19.52]). There the median went from 0.8712 to 0.8226 (-0.0485) and the mean from 0.7701 to 0.7619. active_events found nothing for Patricia: EONET listed 0 open events in 30 days, and widening to 4100 days returned 1 open wildfire from 2025, not the hurricane.
cases.learning: Partly. The imagery side worked: the archive, the scene pick with its reasons, the statistics with a range_note that names the -0.2 offset, and a swipe map. The event side could not help, and that is a finding: active_events reads EONET's open events and GDACS's current-events feed (both named in its notes), so a closed 2015 storm is out of reach at any day count. On the figure, a fall of 0.0485 in the median is small, and the after scene is cloudier (18.53% against 11.6% scene-wide), and cloud lowers the index, so how much of the drop is wind damage and how much is cloud is not separable from these numbers (my reading). The 11.6% before is the cloud for the whole scene, not the box; the screenshot shows cloud over the land on both sides (my reading of the image). The land box still crosses some coast, which I read as why its max is 19.46 and 30.08 (my reading). Not checked: a cloud mask from qa_pixel, the Landsat 7 2015-11-22 pick (4.0% cloud, passed over to keep to one Landsat 8 path and row), and the damage track itself against a published survey.
cases.shows: landsat-c2-l2 on both catalogs for 2015 · same path and row before and after · range_note on an ocean box · median index 0.8712 to 0.8226 on land · active_events holds open events only, no 2015 storm · swipe map

cases.answer: Imagery can show the glacier's surface on a late-summer day, not its ice volume: over the Great Aletsch glacier the mean snow and ice index (NDSI) rose from 0.2108 on 2017-08-23 to 0.2275 on 2026-08-30, +0.0167 (+7.9%), and that is snow cover on the day, not ice volume. The 5% figure is GLAMOS's ground measurement (the Swiss glacier monitoring network, working from stakes, surveys and elevation models), which these tools cannot test, so nothing here speaks for or against "more than 5% of their ice volume in 2026". What the tools can show is the snow and ice at the surface on 1 day each year. From mid August to the end of September under 20% cloud there was 1 scene in 2017 (4.10% cloud) and 10 in 2026; compare_dates picked 2026-08-30 (9.79% cloud) from the same tile, 32TMS, covering 100.0% of the box. The medians are close, 0.1048 and 0.1080. The swipe map shows ice on both sides of the divider, the tongue with its moraine stripes on the 2026 side, and pale patches that look like cloud over the upper left of the 2017 side (my reading of the image).
cases.artifact_label: map: Great Aletsch NDSI swipe, 2017-08-23 against 2026-08-30 ↗
cases.learning: Partly. The tools did their part: 2 matched Sentinel-2 scenes 9 years apart, an NDSI on correctly scaled bands, per-scene statistics, and a swipe map. They could not do what the sentence asks, because ice volume is not something these tools measure, and the card says so rather than letting a rise of 7.9% stand in for an answer. Why the index rose is not in the output; snow on the day, cloud (9.79% in 2026, and NDSI over cloud is not snow), and the box holding rock and forest as well as ice all move a mean like this (my reading). One mean over a 0.15 by 0.15 degree box is also not glacier area: the tools give no count of pixels above a snow threshold, which is the usual way to turn NDSI into extent. A small quirk: on Earth Search the statistics key comes back as b1, not the expression. Not checked: the Rhône glacier, other late-summer dates in 2026 (10 scenes were there), a snow threshold area, and any GLAMOS figure.

cases.answer: Sentinel-2 caught the Eagle Creek fire on both sides: compare_dates picked 2017-08-26 (cloud 0.319339) and 2017-10-05 (cloud 0.260885) from the same tile, 10TER, and the mean burn index (NBR) over the box fell from 0.6415 to 0.4305, -0.211 (-32.9%). The fire's start date, 2017-09-02, is not in the tool output; taking it from outside, the before scene is 7 days ahead of it and the after is 33 days past it. search_imagery found 3 August scenes and 2 October scenes under 20% cloud, all covering 100.0% of the box; compare_dates took the clearest of each and named the runner-up (2017-08-11 and 2017-10-30). compute_statistics on the same 2 scenes gives the same means, a median that fell from 0.7305 to 0.5782, and a percentile_2 that fell from -0.0242 to -0.5044. The index is NBR, (nir-swir22)/(nir+swir22), on scaled bands (scale 0.0001, offset 0). The swipe map shows the 2017-10-05 side with orange and red patches across the hills south of the river, and the 2017-08-26 side green except for the river itself (my reading of the image).
cases.artifact_label: map: Eagle Creek NBR swipe, 2017-08-26 against 2017-10-05 ↗
cases.learning: Works. This is the one card of the 5 where compare_dates fits: it returned 2 sentinel-2-l2a scenes from Earth Search, and here Sentinel-2 reaches 2017. It picked 2 scenes from 1 tile, scaled the bands, returned the delta with no caveat key, and wrote the swipe map. On the figure: the box is 0.25 by 0.15 degrees and holds the Washington shore and the river as well as the burn (my reading of the map), so a drop of 0.211 in the mean is the whole box, not the burn alone. The usual burn-severity measure differences the 2 NBR images pixel by pixel (dNBR), and the tools give a mean per scene, not a per-pixel difference or a burned area. A lower October sun may also move the index a little (my reading). active_events could not help: EONET answered with a server error (500) on both tries, and GDACS listed 0 active events within 30 days inside the box, so the feeds say nothing about 2017 and, with EONET down, not even all-clear today. Not checked: dNBR severity classes, the burned area against the published perimeter, and the scl cloud and shadow band.
